derivations.claim: A degree-$n$ chord diagram is a pairing of $2n$ cyclically ordered endpoints, so only finitely many such diagrams exist. A 4T relation is determined by a background diagram and finitely many endpoint positions, and a 1T relation by one diagram; hence there are finitely many relation vectors. By [F1], each has integer coefficients, so they form the rows of a finite integer matrix $A$. Write $A_n(F):=F^{C_n}/\operatorname{rowspan}_F(A)$ and $W_n(F):=\operatorname{Hom}_F(A_n(F),F)$. Since $k$ has characteristic zero, $\mathbb Q$ embeds in $k$. The rank of $A$ is unchanged by this field extension: a nonzero maximal minor over $\mathbb Q$ remains nonzero in $k$, while every larger minor that vanishes over $\mathbb Q$ still vanishes in $k$. Thus the row space over $k$ is the scalar extension of the rational row space, and $A_n(k)\cong A_n(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$.

The quotient is finite-dimensional, so extending a rational basis and its dual basis gives $W_n(k)\cong W_n(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$. If $n=0$, the sole diagram is the empty diagram and any weight system is its value $c\in k$; the constant invariant $V(K)=c$ has top symbol $c$. For $n>0$, choose a finite $\mathbb Q$-basis $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_d$ of $W_n(\mathbb Q)$; finite-dimensional row reduction chooses this basis without a choice axiom. By [F2], for each $i$ there is a rational-valued finite-type invariant $V_i$ with top symbol $\phi_i$. Write the given weight system as $W=\sum_{i=1}^d a_i\phi_i$ with $a_i\in k$, and define $V=\sum_{i=1}^d a_iV_i$, viewing each rational value in $k$. Linearity of the finite-difference operator gives top symbol $W$. If $W_n(\mathbb Q)=0$, the sum is empty and the zero invariant supplies the zero weight system.

citations.quote:
Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

Let $D,D'$ be regular oriented diagrams of links $L,L'$. If the diagrams
differ by one oriented Reidemeister move or a planar isotopy, the links are
equivalent. The local Reidemeister replacement has a realization supported
in a ball over its move disk, after choosing lifts that agree outside that
ball. Comparing arbitrary realizing links may additionally require changing
their heights away from the move disk.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: To realize a degree-$n$ diagram, take its finite cyclic list of chord endpoints, identify each paired pair as a four-valent vertex, and join consecutive endpoints by arcs in $S^3$. Choose disjoint small vertex balls first. Place the finitely many intervening arcs successively in general position relative to those already placed; two one-dimensional arcs in a three-manifold can be separated by a small endpoint-fixed perturbation, so there are no unintended intersections. Smoothing the joins gives exactly the prescribed double points. In the framed case choose a nonzero normal section along the regular arcs and the two branches at every vertex. To close the section around the parameter circle, cut at one regular parameter; the two endpoint unit normals lie in an oriented two-plane and can be joined because its unit circle is connected. Smooth the finitely many joins. This constructs a zero-free framed representative. The framed branch uses [A1] for the normal-bundle structures.

Let $K,K'$ be representatives of the same diagram. Identify their finite marked graphs and fix matching local models in disjoint vertex balls. Join corresponding edge arcs by a homotopy relative to those balls, and homotope the normal sections over the edge strips, allowing zeroes during the homotopy. A finite relative perturbation makes the coincidence equations for two distinct curve parameters transverse: they are three scalar equations in the two curve parameters and time, so their solutions are isolated. It also makes the normal-section zero equation transverse: it is two scalar equations in the curve parameter and time, so its solutions are isolated. The parameter domains can be made compact after deleting a neighborhood of the diagonal, where each curve is locally embedded; the fixed vertex neighborhoods contain no new events. The higher-codimension loci for tangencies, triple points, degenerate section zeroes, or simultaneous events are avoided by the same finite perturbation. Hence only finitely many isolated double-point or framing-zero events occur. Passing any one event changes $D_nV$ by, up to sign, $D_{n+1}V$ on the object with that extra singularity, which vanishes by type at most $n$ in [F1]. Therefore $D_nV(K)=D_nV(K')$. These are finite-dimensional perturbations of a compact one-parameter family; the framed branch additionally uses [A1], and no countable choice is used in the unframed argument.

For a 4T generator choose the four local singular representatives with the same outside $(n-2)$ marked double points and, in the framed case, the same zero-free framing outside the move ball. Resolving the local marked double point with the positive-minus-negative convention gives $w_V(D_1)=a-b$, $w_V(D_2)=c-d$, $w_V(D_3)=c-a$, and $w_V(D_4)=d-b$, where $a,b,c,d$ are the four values of $D_{n-1}V$ on the remaining local configurations. The repeated configurations are identified by the oriented Reidemeister III isotopies in [F3]: $a$ occurs in the positive resolution of $D_1$ and negative resolution of $D_3$, $b$ in the negative resolutions of $D_1,D_4$, $c$ in the positive resolutions of $D_2,D_3$, and $d$ in the negative resolution of $D_2$ and positive resolution of $D_4$. Their resolution signs follow [F4]. Therefore $w_V(D_1)-w_V(D_2)+w_V(D_3)-w_V(D_4)=(a-b)-(c-d)+(c-a)-(d-b)=0$. The same local calculation applies to zero-free framed representatives because the framing outside the move ball is unchanged. This local calculation is choice-free once the framed objects are defined.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot
$K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$, its normal bundle is
$\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, oriented so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a
positive basis of a normal fibre gives the ambient orientation. A **framing**
of $K$ is a homotopy class through smooth nowhere-zero sections of $\nu K$.
The normal bundle is made a smooth vector bundle under this axiom; a framed
knot includes the section class as data, not a choice made afterwards. For the
relative integer use the round metric transferred from the unit sphere in
$\mathbb R^4$ by the explicit diffeomorphism
$$x\longmapsto\left(\frac{2x}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2},\frac{\lVert x\rVert^2-1}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2}\right),\qquad\infty\longmapsto(0,0,0,1).$$
It induces a smooth bundle metric on $\nu K$. The resulting winding number is
independent of the metric: any two smooth fibre metrics interpolate through
positive metrics and the corresponding angle maps are homotopic.

Given a reference framing $[s_0]$ and another framing $[s_1]$, use a bundle
metric and the positive quarter-turn $J$ on each oriented normal plane. Choose
representatives $s_0,s_1$ and normalize both to unit sections
$\widehat s_i(x):=s_i(x)/\lVert s_i(x)\rVert$. Write
$$\widehat s_1(x)=\cos\theta(x)\widehat s_0(x)+\sin\theta(x)J\widehat s_0(x).$$
The resulting map $S^1\to S^1$ has a continuous angle lift along a parameter
interval $[0,1]$: subdivide into finitely many intervals whose images lie in
open semicircles and choose consecutive local arguments agreeing at endpoints.
Since the map is closed, the lift satisfies $\theta(1)-\theta(0)=2\pi m$ for
some $m\in\mathbb Z$; different lifts differ by a constant multiple of
$2\pi$, and homotopies keep $m$ fixed. Conversely, the difference between
$\theta(t)$ and $\theta(0)+2\pi mt$ is periodic, so linear interpolation of
these angles gives a homotopy to the degree-$m$ rotation of $\widehat s_0$.
Every integer occurs by such a rotation. Thus $m$ classifies the framing class
relative to $[s_0]$ and gives the **relative framing integer**. Once a reference
framing is supplied, the framing classes are an integer torsor; no absolute
integer is assigned before choosing a reference.

The **self-linking number** of a framed knot $(K,[s])$ is the linking number
of $K$ with a sufficiently small push-off along $s$, oriented parallel to $K$.
The push-off and its integer are independent of the representative section,
small radius, and normalized tubular chart by the preceding well-definedness
result.

If a compact oriented surface $\Sigma$ is supplied with boundary $K$, its
**Seifert framing relative to $\Sigma$** is the homotopy class of the inward
unit conormal to $K$ in $\Sigma$, viewed as a nonzero normal section to $K$ in
$S^3$. This definition is relative to the supplied surface; it neither asserts
that every knot bounds such a surface nor asserts the self-linking-zero result.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be an
oriented smooth embedded circle and let $s$ be a smooth nowhere-zero section of
its normal bundle. For any tubular neighbourhood chart that is the inclusion
on the zero section and identifies each vertical normal fibre with the ambient
normal quotient by the identity, the curve $K_{\varepsilon s}$ obtained by
mapping the graph of $\varepsilon s$ into $S^3$ is an embedded oriented circle
disjoint from $K$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. The integer
linking number of $K$ with $K_{\varepsilon s}$ is independent of the sufficiently
small radius, of the representative section in its homotopy class, and of the
normalized tubular chart. It therefore defines a self-linking integer of the
framing class $[s]$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram
of a knot $K$ with blackboard framing $b_D$. The self-linking number of the
framed knot $(K,b_D)$ equals the diagram writhe:
$$\operatorname{sl}(K,b_D)=\operatorname{wr}(D).$$

$L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$, and let $b_{D,i}$ be the blackboard framing
of $K_i$ induced by its component subdiagram. Then
$\operatorname{sl}(K_i,b_{D,i})=\operatorname{wr}_i(D)\qquad(1\le i\le r).$ Total writhe of a link still includes
the signs of mixed crossings, while the sum of component self-linking numbers
uses only self-crossings.

components. If it does not have exactly two components, return

one pass over its finite crossing list. At each crossing whose branches lie on
different components, add
$$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$$
to $s$, where the determinant is taken in the oriented projection plane; ignore
self-crossings. Return $s/2$. The even-sum lemma establishes that this output is
an integer and is the diagram's linking number.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On every finite regular oriented diagram
with exactly two components, the crossing-scan algorithm halts after one
iteration per crossing and returns the integer half-sum of the mixed crossing
signs. On an input with any other number of components it returns
`invalid-input` after the finite component-count check.

derivations.claim: Let $K$ be an $n$-singular knot with an isolated chord corresponding to the double point $p$. Its two preimages split the parameter circle into arcs $A$ and $B$. Isolation means no other marked double point has one preimage on each of $A$ and $B$. Choose a regular projection. There are finitely many ordinary crossings between the arcs. Switch them one at a time until every crossing has the $A$-branch over the $B$-branch. Each switch changes $D_nV$ by, up to sign, the $(n+1)$-fold difference on the knot with that ordinary crossing newly marked; this is zero by [F1]. Thus these switches preserve $D_nV(K)$.

For the framed branch, let $V$ be integer-valued self-linking. On a regular framed diagram compare a unit representative of its framing section $f$ with the unit blackboard normal section $b$. Their oriented fibrewise angle defines a map $S^1\to S^1$; let $\tau(f,b)\in\mathbb Z$ be its degree. In the tubular coordinates determined by $(b,Jb)$, the push-off along $f$ winds $\tau(f,b)$ times meridionally relative to the blackboard push-off. A positive meridian links the core once, since its oriented normal disk meets the core once with the sign fixed by the positive frame $(T,b,Jb)$. Thus $\operatorname{sl}(K,f)=\operatorname{sl}(K,b)+\tau(f,b)$; [F9] supplies the unit-twist normalization, and this local orientation calculation fixes its sign. Equivalently, each positive turn creates a local clasp with two positive mixed crossings, and [F7]–[F8] give the same linking increment. By [F6], $\operatorname{sl}(K,b)=\operatorname{wr}(D)$. For a framed singular knot with two disjoint singularities, all changes outside their local balls are fixed. Inside each ball, resolving a double point changes only that crossing's writhe contribution and local angle path; resolving a framing zero changes only the local angle path. Winding degrees add under concatenation, so the four self-linking values have the form $C+c_1\epsilon_1+c_2\epsilon_2$ for constants independent of $(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$. Their alternating second difference is $(C+c_1+c_2)-(C+c_1-c_2)-(C-c_1+c_2)+(C-c_1-c_2)=0$. This covers any pair of double-point or framing-zero singularities, so self-linking has type at most $1$. On a one-chord diagram with blackboard framing, the two crossing resolutions have writhes $+1$ and $-1$ and zero relative twist; their derivative is $1-(-1)=2$ by [F3] and [F6]. This is nonzero over $\mathbb Z$, so no universal framed 1T vanishing law is valid. The $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption enters only through [F4]–[F9] and [A1].

The consistent over-under assignment lets the lifts of the interiors of $A$ and $B$ lie in opposite open half-spaces bounded by a plane through $p$. Cap each arc on its own side by a short boundary-parallel arc to obtain oriented singular knots $A^\circ$ and $B^\circ$ carrying the remaining marked double points. The two resolutions at $p$ are the connected sums $A^\circ\#B^\circ$ and $B^\circ\#A^\circ$. An orientation-preserving half-turn of the round $S^3$ that exchanges the two balls of the connected-sum decomposition carries the first knot, with its orientation, to the second; the path of rotations through angles from $0$ to $\pi$ is an ambient isotopy. Hence the two resolutions are ambient-isotopic, so their $V$-values agree and $D_nV(K)=0$.

Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $D_0$ and $D_1$ represent the same unframed oriented knot, since they differ by one oriented Reidemeister I move.

The diagram $D_0$ has no crossings, so $w(D_0)=0$. The diagram $D_1$ adds exactly one positive crossing and leaves all other crossings absent, so $w(D_1)=+1$ by [F3]. Therefore writhe is not constant on the ambient-isotopy class of the unknot; by [F2] it cannot be an unframed finite-type knot invariant.

The input is a finite regular oriented link diagram together with its declared
components. If it does not have exactly two components, return
`invalid-input`. For a two-component diagram $D$, initialize $s:=0$ and make
one pass over its finite crossing list. At each crossing whose branches lie on
different components, add
$$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$$
to $s$, where the determinant is taken in the oriented projection plane; ignore
self-crossings. Return $s/2$. The even-sum lemma establishes that this output is
an integer and is the diagram's linking number.

with exactly two components, the crossing-scan algorithm halts after one
iteration per crossing and returns the integer half-sum of the mixed crossing
signs. On an input with any other number of components it returns
`invalid-input` after the finite component-count check.

of ambient-isotopic two-component links, the algorithmic linking numbers
agree. Creating a positive type-I kink increases total writhe by $1$ and
deleting it decreases writhe by $1$; creating a negative kink decreases writhe
by $1$ and deleting it increases writhe by $1$. Types II and III leave total
writhe unchanged. For a knot
component, blackboard self-linking changes by the same amount under a type-I
move. Consequently writhe and blackboard self-linking are not invariants of
unframed ambient isotopy, although the integer linking number of two distinct
components is.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Let $C$ be half the signed sum of all mixed crossings except the marked one. Under [A1], [F4] identifies the diagram half-sum with the integer linking number and [F5] makes it an ambient-isotopy invariant. By [F2] and [F3], the positive and negative resolutions contribute respectively $+\tfrac12$ and $-\tfrac12$ to this linking number, so $\operatorname{lk}(L_1,L_2)_+-\operatorname{lk}(L_1,L_2)_-=(C+\tfrac12)-(C-\tfrac12)=1$. This is the stated positive-minus-negative derivative under [F1]; reversing that subtraction changes its sign.
A knot has one component and therefore no unordered pair of distinct components; the total pairwise linking sum contains no terms and equals $0$.

If both marked crossings are mixed, write their resolution signs as $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\{+1,-1\}$ and absorb every other mixed crossing into $C$. By [F2]–[F4], $\operatorname{lk}(L_{\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2})=C+\tfrac12(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)$. The alternating second difference is zero: the constant has coefficient $1-1-1+1=0$, and each term linear in one $\epsilon_i$ cancels when the other sign is summed. If either marked crossing is a self-crossing, the link formula [F3] is independent of that resolution, so the alternating sum over its two choices cancels term by term. Thus $D_2=0$ for every pair of marked crossings by [F1].
